function: Excluded as above_phy: the learned Co-HDRL decides base-station sleep on/off and transmit-power levels for energy-efficient RAN management (pp. 4-5); RIS phase shifts come from non-learned fractional programming (p. 9).
notes: Reason above_phy. The learned part is a hierarchical double-DQN: p. 5: "The MBS is defined as a meta-controller for sleep control, which decides the long-term on/off status of attached SBSs", and each SBS sub-controller adjusts its "short-term transmission power level". This is RAN energy management; p. 13 calls it "network management" and "RAN management". The RIS is not learned: p. 9: "approach is applied to optimize RIS phase shifts" (Section V-A, fractional programming), and p. 10: "the RIS optimization module can be considered as part of the environment reward function"; the surrogate-optimization baseline is also non-learned. No beamforming, detection or channel estimation is learned. If a reviewer reads the learned transmit-power control as a physical-layer decision, the work still fails the function check, since neither sleep control nor power control is one of the seven areas (area 3 needs learned precoder, beams or RIS phase shifts). The evaluation is a custom MATLAB simulation with 6 RISs of 10 elements (pp. 10-11) and Rician RIS-UE fading (p. 3); no code link is given.
